subject: Next steps: data retention SLAs & log policy (backup impact)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ho <alex.ho@medisolve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: data retention SLAs & log policy (backup impact)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap (30 min):
- Primary ask: confirmation of Redwood's data deletion and log retention behavior for HIPAA-bound PHI and PII.
- Audit requirement: evidence that deletion requests are honored across primary stores and how backups are handled.
- SOC 2: you asked about our current coverage and timeline for Type II.

What I can do / immediate answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently undergoing our first SOC 2 Type II audit (in fieldwork). Expected completion Q3 2027; we can share the SOC 2 report once finalized and signed by the auditor.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support processing under standard contracts; for HIPAA we provide BAAs for customers that need them.
- Deletion SLA (high level): we typically remove customer data from active serving copies within 24–72 hours after a validated deletion request. Backups are handled by retention windows — default backup retention is 180 days, but we can work with you on a shorter policy for enterprise contracts; there are some technical/operational caveats I call out below.
- Logs: request traces and access/audit logs are kept 90 days by default; longer retention (up to 365 days) is available for enterprise customers.

Outstanding for us to provide:
1) A short retention matrix that maps data types (primary data, backups, KV cache, logs, analytics) to default and configurable retention windows (attaching a first draft).
2) Vendor security questionnaire — we can start that and send the XLSX for your security team to complete.
3) A technical 45-minute workshop to walk through backup architecture and deletion proof for auditors.

Attachments: retention_matrix.pdf (draft)

Next steps:
- Ben (cc) will drop the vendor security questionnaire to you once you confirm preferred format.
- Rafael (cc) can run the technical workshop next week; please suggest a couple of 45-minute slots.
- Alex: please confirm if you require backups to be purged within 30 days for your HIPAA controls — that will determine whether we need an exception to our default retention windows or a special archival workflow.

Thanks — happy to tighten language for procurement/audit evidence.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Next steps: data retention SLAs & log policy (backup impact)

Grace —

Appreciate the recap. A couple clarifying items from Medisolve security: 

1) For HIPAA we need an enforceable contract clause that data subject deletion (e.g., patient record removal) results in removal from all customer-accessible and vendor-managed copies within 30 days. For backups, auditors understand a window, but we need a clear timeline and proof that the data is not recoverable after that window.
2) Can you provide a short paragraph we can include in our security appendix describing the deletion pipeline (how deletion requests propagate to primary and backup stores)?
3) Please send the vendor security questionnaire (XLSX) for our security team — we'll turn it around in 3–5 business days.

Also, are there specific limitations around immutable backups (snapshots) where data cannot be removed until the snapshot expires? That's a common concern for our InfoSec.

If possible, we prefer a 30-day overall eradication guarantee for HIPAA data (primary + backups). If that requires contract exceptions, please flag it now so we can start procurement conversations.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ho
Security Lead, MediSolve
alex.ho@medisolve.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: data retention SLAs & log policy (backup impact)

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a more explicit description you can include in your appendix, and a proposed SLA we can discuss with procurement.

Short paragraph for appendix (draft):
Redwood Inference processes customer data in separate primary serving stores and periodic immutable backups. Upon receiving a validated deletion request, Redwood removes the data from active serving copies within 24–72 hours. Backups are retained according to the contractually agreed retention window; Redwood will remove data from backup copies when the backup retention window elapses or via a secure purge process for short-retention contracts. Proof of deletion can be provided via deletion logs and backup purge records; Redwood can supply a deletion attest report for auditor review.

Proposed deletion SLA (subject to enterprise contract terms):
- Active copies: removal initiated on validated request, completed within 48 hours.
- Primary backups / short-term snapshots: removal or tombstone marking completed within 30 days post-request (subject to snapshot lifecycle).
- Long-term archive retention (if used): up to 180 days by default; shorter retention can be negotiated for enterprise customers.

Notes and caveats:
- Immutable snapshot windows: some backup systems create point-in-time, immutable snapshots. For those, we mark the data as logically deleted (tombstone) immediately and prevent restoration to customer-accessible systems; physical purging will follow the snapshot lifecycle (we can shorten lifecycle under contract but may require operational lead time).
- Proof: we provide deletion logs, backup purge manifests, and an engineer-signed attestation.

I've attached the vendor security questionnaire for your team to fill out (vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx). Ben, could you confirm we want the security team to return the completed XLSX to security@redwood.com?

Finally, Rafael and I can run the technical workshop — Rafael can cover backup architecture and tombstone/proof mechanics. Rafael: any quick additions?

Best,
Grace

Subject: Re: Next steps: data retention SLAs & log policy (backup impact)

Alex / Grace —

Quick technical notes to supplement Grace's answers: 

1) Logs vs. primary data: audit and request traces are stored separately from customer data blobs. PII in logs is redacted by default; where full request payloads are retained, we can scope retention to 90 days (default) or extend to up to 365 days on enterprise plans.

2) Backups / snapshots: our warm backups use incremental snapshots; immutable snapshots are retained until their lifecycle end. For customers requiring 30-day full-eradication, we implement a short-retention backup policy and an expedited purge workflow:
   - Mark object as deleted across indexes immediately.
   - Trigger metadata purge from backup catalog within 7 days.
   - Physical expunge follows snapshot expiration (configurable; can be forced under contract with an operational maintenance window).

3) Attestation and proofs we can provide: deletion logs, backup purge manifest (hashes and timestamps), and a signed attestation for auditors.

4) Playbook offer: attached is a short playbook that describes the deletion playbook we run during a removal request (redwood_deletion_playbook.md). I recommend a 45-minute technical workshop with your engineers and InfoSec to walk through how we generate proof for auditors and what we can commit to contractually.

Suggested slots: Thurs 2027-05-20 10:00–10:45 PT or Fri 2027-05-21 13:00–13:45 PT. Alex — which works for you?

Attachments: redwood_deletion_playbook.md

Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
